Accountable obligation owner.value: Designated PIPA privacy officer under PIPA s.4; escalation to the Data Protection Officer and Privacy Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Bermuda Personal Information Protection Act 2016 ss.4-6 (privacy officer, fair processing, conditions for use) as in full force since 1 January 2025, re-read against the PrivCom Bermuda published text at each annual register review

In-scope processes.value: Every process that uses personal information of policyholders, claimants, beneficiaries, producers and employees — underwriting, policy admin, claims, complaints, marketing, HR — each captured as a processing activity in the register with its lawful condition of use

In-scope systems.value: Processing register maintained in the data catalog, cross-referenced to CMDB applications holding personal information; register exports filed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Records of Processing Procedure — intake trigger for new systems/vendors/initiatives, activity capture fields, PIPA s.6 condition-of-use selection guide, overseas-transfer flags, quarterly attestation cycle

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Data Protection Officer and Head of Compliance; re-approved annually and on any PIPA amendment or PrivCom guidance note

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous obligation — no external filing; internal deadlines are the quarterly business-owner attestation (calendar quarter end + 15 business days) and the annual full register review each January

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC workflow reminders at T-10 and T-3 business days before each quarterly attestation close, and a 1 December reminder to open the annual register review

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Quarterly register snapshots, attestation records and lawful-basis worksheets retained 6 years in the compliance evidence repository, aligned to Bermuda limitation periods

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any processing activity found live without a register entry or without a named PIPA s.6 condition is logged as a privacy exception with root cause, remediation owner and date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The DPO signs off closure of every register-gap exception and every lawful-basis re-determination

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All applications flagged in the CMDB as holding personal information, plus all register entries and all new systems/vendors onboarded in the review period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any personal-information system with no register entry is a fail; any register entry with a blank or unsupported s.6 condition of use is a fail; >2% of sampled entries failing escalates to the DPO and Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the register completeness and lawful-basis test runs annually with a quarterly spot-check of new onboardings

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the Privacy Office and must not have authored any sampled register entry

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual PIPA register test workpaper (CMDB extract, register reconciliation, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Privacy/PIPA/Register

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Current register export with lawful conditions, transfer flags and privacy-notice cross-references, producible to PrivCom Bermuda within 5 business days of an information request

Regulator response path.value: The Privacy Officer fronts any PrivCom Bermuda inquiry; Privacy Counsel clears responses that concede a register gap before release; BMA questions raised in a prudential review route via Regulatory Counsel

checklist.step: Confirm the designated privacy officer and the register's operating mandate
actions: Check the board or delegated-authority minute that designates the PIPA s.4 privacy officer names the current incumbent; if stale, route a refreshed designation to the Corporate Secretary for the next committee sitting.
Publish the privacy officer's name and contact route on the intranet privacy page and in the external privacy notice, as PIPA requires the officer to be reachable for individuals' requests.
Record the designation date and minute reference in the GRC platform under the PIPA obligation record.
checklist.done: a current, minuted privacy-officer designation exists and the officer is named in the published privacy notice.

checklist.step: Pull the system universe that can hold personal information
actions: Export from the CMDB every application with the data-classification attribute set to 'Personal' or 'Sensitive Personal', including SaaS entries.
Ask the Chief Information Officer's application owners to confirm the export misses nothing — new SaaS bought on purchasing cards is the classic gap.
Reconcile the export against the data catalog's scanned sources and against the vendor list from Procurement for data-touching services.
Freeze the reconciled universe as this cycle's scope list and file it in the register folder.
checklist.done: a reconciled, dated system universe list exists and every difference between CMDB, catalog and vendor list is resolved or logged.

checklist.step: Capture one register entry per processing activity
actions: For each in-scope system, sit with the business owner and break usage into discrete processing activities (e.g. 'life new-business underwriting', 'claims beneficiary payment', 'marketing re-engagement').

Complete the register fields per activity: purpose, categories of individuals, categories of personal information, sensitive personal information flag (PIPA s.7), source of the data, recipients, and the system(s) involved.
Record the retention period per activity from the corporate retention schedule, and flag any activity with no schedule entry to the Records Manager.
Mark activities that disclose data to an overseas third party for the transfer review step.
checklist.done: every in-scope system maps to at least one complete register entry with no blank purpose, category or retention field.

checklist.step: Assign the PIPA s.6 condition of use to every activity
actions: For each register entry, select the lawful condition from PIPA s.6: consent, contract performance, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, or the reasonableness/legitimate-interest style condition — and write the specific justification sentence, not just the label.
Where consent is the condition, name where the consent record lives (application form clause, portal tick-box, recorded call) and how it is withdrawn.
Where sensitive personal information is processed, verify a s.7-compatible basis and record it separately on the entry.
Reject entries where the steward proposed 'consent' for processing that actually rests on the insurance contract — mislabelled bases fail PrivCom scrutiny.
checklist.done: every register entry carries a named s.6 condition with a written justification, and sensitive-data entries carry a s.7 basis.

checklist.step: Review overseas transfers and third-party disclosures
actions: For each entry flagged as disclosing personal information to an overseas third party, record the receiving country and the PIPA s.15 mechanism relied on — comparable level of protection assessment or contractual safeguards.
Cross-check that the receiving vendor's contract contains the data-protection clauses required by the vendor-contract obligation (REG-054-C26) and note the contract reference on the register entry.
Where no mechanism is documented, open a privacy exception in the GRC platform and stop new transfers until Privacy Counsel signs a basis.
checklist.done: every overseas-transfer entry names the destination, the s.15 mechanism and the contract reference, or carries an open exception.

checklist.step: Cross-check the register against the published privacy notices
actions: Read the external privacy notice and the employee privacy notice side-by-side with the register export.
Confirm every register purpose is described in a notice, and every notice statement traces to a real register entry — notices promising less than the register does are a PIPA s.9 clarity failure.
Log wording gaps as notice-change requests with an owner and a publication date.
checklist.done: purposes in the register and statements in the notices reconcile both ways, with change requests raised for any gap.

checklist.step: Wire the intake trigger so new processing lands in the register before go-live
actions: Add a mandatory 'personal information?' question to the project intake form in the PPM tool and to the Procurement vendor-onboarding form; a Yes routes a register task to the Privacy Office automatically.
Configure the GRC workflow so the register task must close before the project or vendor record can reach 'approved' status.
Brief the PMO Analyst and Procurement Specialist communities on the gate at their next chapter meeting and file the deck.
checklist.done: intake forms carry the trigger question and the GRC workflow blocks approval until the register task closes.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly business-owner attestation
actions: Within 15 business days of each quarter end, issue each business owner their register entries via GRC attestation campaign.
Each owner confirms per entry: still active, purpose unchanged, no new recipients, no new overseas transfer — or flags the change.
Chase non-responders at T-10 and T-3 days; escalate remaining non-responses to the Head of Compliance.
Apply flagged changes to the register the same quarter and route new lawful-basis questions to Privacy Counsel.
checklist.done: 100% of register entries are attested or escalated each quarter, and flagged changes are applied with dated edits.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to the data catalog scans
actions: Run the catalog's classification scan over connected sources and list tables/columns tagged as personal information.
Match each hit to a register entry; a scanned personal-data store with no register entry is a candidate shadow-processing finding.
Confirm candidates with the system owner, then either create the missing entry or reclassify the false positive with a note.
Log genuine misses as privacy exceptions with root cause (intake bypassed, legacy system, scan gap).
checklist.done: every scanned personal-data store maps to a register entry or a dispositioned false positive, with misses logged as exceptions.

checklist.step: Remediate entries with missing or failed lawful bases
actions: Work the exception queue: for each entry lacking a defensible s.6 condition, decide with Privacy Counsel to (a) document the correct basis, (b) obtain consent, or (c) stop the processing and purge per the retention schedule.
Set a remediation date within 60 days of the finding and name the business owner accountable.
Where processing is stopped, confirm with the system owner that the data flow is actually severed, not just the register edited.
checklist.done: every lawful-basis exception has a chosen remedy, an owner, a date within 60 days, and stopped flows are verified severed.

checklist.step: Handle breach-handling and safeguards cross-references on the register
actions: For each register entry, link the safeguard profile: encryption at rest/in transit, access-control group, and the PIPA s.13 proportionality note matching data sensitivity.
Confirm sensitive-personal-information entries reference an access review in the IAM platform within the last 12 months; request one from the Access Management Analyst where missing.
Note the incident-response runbook reference so a breach touching this activity can be scoped fast (feeds REG-054-C28).
checklist.done: each entry links a safeguard profile and sensitive entries evidence a ≤12-month-old access review.

checklist.step: Publish the register health report to privacy governance
actions: Compile quarterly: entry count, new entries, attestation completion %, open exceptions by age, overseas-transfer count by mechanism, and lawful-basis mix.
Present at the privacy governance committee; minute decisions on aged exceptions.
Send the DPO a written summary flagging anything that would embarrass the company in a PrivCom inspection.
checklist.done: a minuted quarterly register health report exists with decisions recorded against every exception older than 90 days.

checklist.step: Run the annual full register review each January
actions: Re-run the system universe pull, re-validate every entry's condition of use with Privacy Counsel, and retire entries for decommissioned processing.
Re-read PIPA and current PrivCom Bermuda guidance for changes affecting condition selection or register content, and record the review note.
Version the register as the annual baseline snapshot.
checklist.done: a dated annual baseline snapshot exists with a review note confirming the legal texts were re-checked.

checklist.step: Keep the regulator-ready export current
actions: Maintain a formatted register export (activities, purposes, conditions, transfers, notice references) refreshed at least quarterly in the compliance evidence repository.
Dry-run the 5-business-day production drill once a year: from a simulated PrivCom request to a clean export handed to Privacy Counsel.
Record the drill result and fix any assembly friction found.
checklist.done: a ≤1-quarter-old export sits in the repository and the annual production drill met the 5-business-day target.

checklist.step: Retain register evidence for the full retention period
actions: File each quarterly snapshot, attestation campaign record and lawful-basis worksheet under Privacy/PIPA/Register with the 6-year retention label.
Verify the repository index retrieves snapshots by quarter and by system name.
Confirm deletion holds are applied where any entry is subject to litigation or a PrivCom inquiry.
checklist.done: snapshots and attestations are filed, labelled for 6-year retention and retrievable by quarter and system.

testing.step: Build the population of personal-information systems and register entries
actions: Extract from the CMDB all applications classified 'Personal'/'Sensitive Personal' as at the test date, and separately export the full processing register.
Add the year's vendor onboardings from Procurement and project go-lives from the PPM tool as potential new processing.
Sign the combined population as complete, noting extract dates and row counts.
testing.done: a dated population of systems, register entries and new onboardings exists with recorded counts.

testing.step: Reconcile systems to register entries both ways
actions: Match every personal-information system to at least one register entry; unmatched systems are automatic completeness exceptions.
Match every register entry to a live system or a documented manual process; orphan entries indicate a stale register.
Run the data catalog scan results against the register as an independent third source and list scan-only hits.
testing.done: every system, entry and scan hit is matched or listed as an exception — no unexplained rows remain.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of register entries
actions: Take 100% of entries flagged as sensitive personal information or overseas transfer.
Add 25 entries selected at random (seeded, reproducible) from the remainder, minimum 40 in total.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all sensitive and transfer entries is drawn and documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the s.6 condition-of-use judgement on each sampled entry
actions: Read the entry's purpose and data categories, then reach your own PIPA s.6 condition conclusion before looking at the recorded one.
Compare to the recorded condition; a different condition, or a justification that merely restates the label, is an exception.
For consent-based entries, request the actual consent artifact (form clause, tick-box config, call recording) and check it covers the stated purpose.
testing.done: each sampled entry has an independent condition re-performance note and consent entries trace to a real consent artifact.

testing.step: Trace sampled entries to privacy notices and retention schedules
actions: Find each sampled purpose in the published privacy notice; an undisclosed purpose is a s.9 exception.
Check the entry's retention period against the corporate retention schedule entry it cites.
Ask the Records Manager for evidence that at least one purge ran per the stated retention for a sampled activity.
testing.done: sampled purposes appear in the notices, retention values match the schedule, and a purge trace exists.

testing.step: Verify overseas-transfer mechanisms on the transfer subsample
actions: For each transfer entry, open the cited vendor contract in the CLM and confirm the data-protection clauses exist and are executed.
Confirm the s.15 mechanism note (comparable protection assessment or contractual safeguards) is documented and dated before the transfer began.
List transfers relying on an undocumented 'we trust them' basis as exceptions.
testing.done: every sampled transfer traces to an executed contract and a dated s.15 mechanism note.

testing.step: Test the intake gate with the year's onboardings
actions: For 10 vendor onboardings and 10 project go-lives from the period, check the intake form's personal-information question was answered and, where Yes, a register task closed before approval.
Compare the register-entry creation date to the go-live date; entries created after go-live are gate failures.
Screenshot the GRC workflow history for each tested record into the workpaper.
testing.done: tested onboardings show the gate fired and register entries pre-date go-live, or failures are logged.

testing.step: Recompute attestation coverage and timeliness
actions: From the GRC campaign records, recompute quarterly attestation completion % against the register entry count for each of the last 4 quarters.
Check campaigns closed within 15 business days of quarter end and escalations fired for non-responders.
Verify flagged changes from attestations landed as register edits in the same quarter.
testing.done: recomputed completion rates match reported figures and flagged changes trace to dated register edits.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception: missing entry, wrong condition, undisclosed purpose, undocumented transfer, or gate bypass.
Assign root cause (intake bypassed, legacy migration, steward error, counsel backlog) and a named owner.
Set remediation dates within 60 days and mark repeat findings from the prior year's test for DPO attention.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and a ≤60-day remediation date, with repeats flagged.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the sample failure rate against the 2% threshold and state a conclusion: register complete and lawful, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the Data Protection Officer review the factual accuracy, then have the Chief Audit Executive — who performed no register work — sign the workpaper.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and present results at the privacy governance committee's next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date sits in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the outsourcing/data-sharing clause gate; escalation to Legal Counsel and, for BMA-facing questions, Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — BMA Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) s.7 outsourcing service-agreement terms (roles, governance, BMA oversight and access to the outsourced function and records), plus PIPA 2016 s.10 for personal-information processors, re-read at each clause-library refresh

In-scope processes.value: Procurement vendor onboarding, contract negotiation and renewal for every material outsourcing arrangement and every vendor or partner that receives company or policyholder data, including intra-group service agreements

In-scope systems.value: Contracts authored and stored in Icertis CLM; sourcing events in Coupa/Ariba; executed copies in the contract lifecycle management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Outsourcing & Data-Sharing Contract Procedure — materiality classification per Code s.7, mandatory clause checklist (BMA access/audit, governance, subcontracting consent, termination/exit, PIPA s.10 data terms), deviation approval path

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the General Counsel and Head of Compliance; refreshed annually and on any BMA Code revision or outsourcing guidance note

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per vendor — clause checklist must close before contract execution; material outsourcing arrangements are notified to the BMA before commencement per the Code's prudential expectations; legacy remediation tracked to a board-approved completion date

Deadline reminders configured.value: CLM renewal alerts at T-120/T-90/T-60 days before each material contract's expiry so clauses are re-verified at renewal; GRC reminder for the annual material-vendor list review each Q1

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Executed contracts, clause checklists, deviation approvals and BMA notification letters retained for contract life + 6 years in the contract lifecycle management repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any executed material or data-sharing contract missing a mandatory clause is logged as a compliance exception with a remediation amendment date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Legal Counsel signs off every clause deviation and every remediation amendment before the exception closes

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All active vendor and data-sharing contracts in the CLM as at the test date, reconciled to accounts-payable spend and the outsourcing register, flagged material/non-material

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any material outsourcing contract without the BMA access/audit clause is a fail; any personal-data contract without PIPA s.10 terms is a fail; ≥1 material-contract fail escalates to the General Counsel and Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-vendor at execution and renewal; the clause-coverage test runs annually over the active book with 100% coverage of contracts executed or renewed in the year

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have negotiated or approved any sampled contract

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual outsourcing-contract test workpaper (CLM extract, AP reconciliation, sample, clause re-reads, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Vendor/Code-s7

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Outsourcing register with per-contract clause status, BMA notification letters and executed contract copies, producible to the BMA within 5 business days of a prudential-review request

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Counsel fronts BMA correspondence on outsourcing arrangements; the Third-Party Risk Manager supplies the register; admissions of a missing-clause contract are cleared by the General Counsel before release

checklist.step: Maintain the mandatory clause library and checklist
actions: Draft and keep current in the CLM clause library the mandatory set: BMA right of oversight, access to the outsourced function and its records (Code s.7); definition of roles, responsibilities and service governance; sub-outsourcing only with consent; audit and inspection rights; termination and orderly exit; business-continuity cooperation; and PIPA s.10 processing terms (purpose limitation, safeguards, breach notice to the company, return/destruction).
Re-read Code s.7 and current BMA outsourcing expectations annually and after any Code revision; record the review note on the library entry.
Version each clause with an effective date so testers can tell which wording applied to which contract.
checklist.done: the CLM clause library holds the current mandatory set with dated versions and an annual legal review note.

checklist.step: Classify every new arrangement for materiality under Code s.7
actions: Score each sourcing request against the materiality criteria: criticality to insurance operations (policy admin, claims, actuarial, IT hosting), data sensitivity, substitutability and concentration.
Record the classification (material outsourcing / data-sharing / ordinary supply) with rationale in the GRC third-party record.
Route material classifications to the Head of Compliance for confirmation before contracting starts.
Add confirmed material arrangements to the outsourcing register with the intended service commencement date.
checklist.done: every sourcing request carries a recorded, confirmed materiality classification before contract drafting begins.

checklist.step: Gate the procurement flow so contracting cannot skip the clause checklist
actions: Configure the Coupa/Ariba sourcing workflow so any request tagged material or data-sharing cannot advance to contract award until the CLM clause checklist task is attached and marked complete.
Block purchase-order creation against vendors whose GRC record shows classification pending.
Brief Procurement Specialists that side-letters and clickwrap SaaS terms count as contracts and must enter the same gate.
checklist.done: the sourcing workflow demonstrably blocks award and PO creation until the clause checklist closes.

checklist.step: Negotiate the mandatory clauses into the draft contract
actions: Author the draft in the CLM from the standard template so mandatory clauses are present by default; for vendor-paper deals, run the CLM clause-comparison against the library and list every missing or diluted clause.
Negotiate the BMA access/audit clause as non-waivable for material outsourcing — the BMA must be able to obtain information from and about the outsourced function and its records on request.
Complete the clause checklist in the CLM, marking each mandatory clause present/absent with the contract section reference.
Send unresolved vendor pushback on mandatory clauses to Legal Counsel rather than trading the clause away.
checklist.done: the draft carries every mandatory clause with checklist section references, or open pushback sits with Legal Counsel.

checklist.step: Add PIPA s.10 data-processing terms for any personal-information flow
actions: Where the register (REG-054-C25) shows the vendor will use personal information, attach the data-processing addendum: process only on documented instructions, PIPA s.13-proportionate safeguards, notify the company of any breach of security without undue delay, no sub-processing without consent, return or destroy data at exit.
For overseas vendors, document the PIPA s.15 transfer mechanism on the contract record and cross-reference the processing register entry.
Initial the addendum on the clause checklist so testers can trace privacy terms separately from commercial terms.
checklist.done: every personal-data contract carries the executed s.10 addendum and, for overseas vendors, a documented s.15 mechanism.

checklist.step: Obtain deviation approval where a mandatory clause is genuinely unobtainable
actions: Document the deviation: which clause, the vendor's position, the residual risk and the compensating control (e.g. escrow, enhanced monitoring, alternative audit route).
For material outsourcing, deviations from the BMA access clause are not approvable — record the rule and reroute the deal or the vendor.
Obtain written approval from the General Counsel and the Head of Compliance and attach it to the CLM record with an expiry/review date.
checklist.done: every deviation is documented, approved in writing with a review date, and no material contract deviates on BMA access.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA before a material outsourcing commences
actions: Prepare the BMA notification for each new material outsourcing: the function outsourced, the provider, jurisdictions, materiality rationale, governance and exit arrangements.
Submit through the BMA's e-filing channel or by letter to the supervisory contact before the service commencement date, and diarise any BMA questions for response within the timeframe the BMA sets.
File the notification and any BMA acknowledgement on the outsourcing register entry and in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: each material arrangement shows a pre-commencement BMA notification with the filed acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Execute and store the contract with its checklist
actions: Route the final contract for signature via DocuSign using the delegated-authority signing matrix; reject signatures from staff outside the matrix.
File the fully executed copy, the completed clause checklist and any deviation approvals into the contract lifecycle management repository, indexed by vendor, materiality flag and expiry date.
Update the outsourcing register entry to 'executed' with the effective and expiry dates.
checklist.done: the executed contract, checklist and approvals are filed and the register entry shows executed status with dates.

checklist.step: Remediate legacy contracts missing mandatory clauses
actions: Run the CLM clause-comparison over the legacy active book and list every material or data-sharing contract missing a mandatory clause.
Prioritise by materiality and expiry: remediate material contracts by amendment now; queue non-material ones for the next renewal.
Track each amendment to countersignature and close the corresponding GRC exception only when the executed amendment is filed.
Report the remediation burn-down monthly to the Head of Compliance until the backlog clears.
checklist.done: a prioritised legacy gap list exists, material gaps are amended, and the burn-down is reported monthly.

checklist.step: Re-verify clauses at every renewal
actions: Act on CLM renewal alerts at T-120 days: re-run the clause checklist against the current library version, since the library may have moved on since first execution.
Treat auto-renewing contracts as renewals — intercept before the auto-renew date rather than after.
Log any clause now missing as a renewal-blocking item for the Contracts Manager.
checklist.done: every renewal (including auto-renewals) shows a re-run checklist against the current clause library.

checklist.step: Exercise the access and audit rights on material vendors
actions: Schedule at least one audit-rights exercise per year across the material vendor population (on-site, remote evidence review, or SOC report walkthrough with follow-up questions).
Confirm during the exercise that the vendor could produce records to the BMA on request — ask for the records-retrieval demonstration, not just a policy statement.
Record findings and remediation actions on the vendor's GRC record.
checklist.done: at least one documented rights exercise ran in the year and each finding carries an owner and date.

checklist.step: Maintain the outsourcing register as the single source of truth
actions: Keep one register row per arrangement: vendor, function, materiality, contract reference, clause-checklist status, BMA notification date, data flag, expiry, and exit-plan reference.
Reconcile the register quarterly to the CLM active-contract list and to AP spend over the materiality threshold to catch contracts signed outside the gate.
Review the material-vendor list annually each Q1 with the Third-Party Risk Manager and re-confirm classifications.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to CLM and AP quarterly and the Q1 materiality re-confirmation is minuted.

checklist.step: Report outsourcing posture to governance
actions: Present quarterly to the risk committee: material arrangements, new BMA notifications, clause exceptions and deviations in force, remediation burn-down, and audit-rights findings.
Minute committee decisions on any deviation extension or concentration concern.
Include outsourcing posture in the annual Code-of-Conduct compliance assessment presented to the board.
checklist.done: quarterly committee packs and minutes cover the register, exceptions and deviations, and the annual board assessment includes outsourcing.

checklist.step: Log and disposition every contract exception
actions: Raise a GRC exception for any executed contract found missing a mandatory clause, any gate bypass, and any material arrangement that commenced before its BMA notification.
Assign root cause (vendor paper accepted unreviewed, gate bypassed via P-card, legacy migration) and a named owner.
For commencement-before-notification cases, assess with Regulatory Counsel whether a self-report under the Code's non-compliance provisions is required (feeds REG-054-C30).
checklist.done: every exception carries root cause, owner, remediation date, and notification breaches carry a self-report assessment.

checklist.step: Retain contract evidence for the full retention period
actions: Apply the contract-life-plus-6-years retention label to executed contracts, checklists, deviation approvals and BMA notifications.
Verify retrieval by vendor name, materiality flag and clause status for exam-readiness.
Apply holds where a vendor dispute or regulatory inquiry is open.
checklist.done: contract evidence is labelled, retrievable by vendor and clause status, and holds are applied where required.

testing.step: Build the population of active contracts and arrangements
actions: Extract all active contracts from the CLM as at the test date with materiality and data flags.
Extract 12 months of AP spend by vendor and list vendors above the materiality spend threshold with no CLM contract — candidate off-register arrangements.
Pull the outsourcing register and record all three counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: CLM, AP and register extracts are dated and counted, with off-register candidates listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to CLM and AP
actions: Match every register row to an executed CLM contract; unmatched rows are register-integrity exceptions.
Match every above-threshold AP vendor to a register row or a documented non-material rationale; unmatched vendors are gate-bypass candidates.
Confirm bypass candidates with Procurement and classify each as a genuine bypass or a false positive with evidence.
testing.done: all three sources reconcile with every difference dispositioned as an exception or an evidenced false positive.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of material outsourcing contracts and 100% of contracts executed or renewed in the test year.
Add 15 randomly selected (seeded, reproducible) non-material data-sharing contracts.
Record seed, population and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all material and in-year contracts plus a reproducible non-material selection.

testing.step: Re-read each sampled contract for the mandatory clauses
actions: Open the executed PDF — not the template — and locate each mandatory clause: BMA oversight/access to the function and records, roles and governance, sub-outsourcing consent, audit rights, termination/exit, and (where data flows) the PIPA s.10 addendum.
Record the section reference found for each clause and compare against the contract's clause checklist; a checklist claiming a clause the executed text lacks is an exception in its own right.
Treat diluted wording (e.g. audit rights 'subject to vendor consent') as absent unless a deviation approval is attached.
testing.done: every sampled contract has a clause-by-clause re-read with section references reconciled to its checklist.

testing.step: Re-perform the materiality classification on the sample
actions: Apply the Code s.7 materiality criteria to each sampled arrangement without reference to the recorded classification.
Compare conclusions; an arrangement you would call material that was classified ordinary supply is an exception with immediate escalation, since it likely skipped BMA notification.
Note borderline calls and check they carry a Head of Compliance confirmation.
testing.done: independent materiality conclusions are recorded and any under-classification is escalated.

testing.step: Trace BMA notifications for material arrangements
actions: For each material arrangement, retrieve the BMA notification letter or e-filing receipt from the evidence repository.
Compare the notification date to the service commencement date; commencement first is a reportable breach, not a documentation gap.
Verify any BMA follow-up questions were answered within the timeframe the BMA set.
testing.done: every material arrangement shows a pre-commencement notification and closed BMA follow-ups, or a logged breach.

testing.step: Verify deviation approvals and their boundaries
actions: For every sampled contract with a missing or diluted clause, retrieve the deviation approval and check it names the clause, the compensating control, the approvers and a review date.
Confirm no deviation exists against the BMA access clause on a material contract — any such approval is itself an exception.
Check expired deviations were re-reviewed or remediated.
testing.done: all deviations are properly approved, none touch BMA access on material contracts, and expiries were actioned.

testing.step: Test the procurement gate end to end
actions: For 10 in-year awards, pull the Coupa/Ariba workflow history and confirm the clause-checklist task closed before award and PO creation.
Attempt (in a test client or by configuration review) to advance a material-tagged request without the checklist; the workflow must block it.
Screenshot workflow histories and the block behaviour into the workpaper.
testing.done: workflow histories show the gate held for sampled awards and the block behaviour is evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception: missing clause, checklist misstatement, under-classification, late/absent BMA notification, gate bypass.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date; missing-clause fixes get a target amendment date.
Route commencement-before-notification and under-classification findings to Regulatory Counsel for the self-report assessment under REG-054-C30.
testing.done: every exception is logged with cause, owner and date, and regulatory-notification breaches carry a self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute fail counts against the thresholds (zero tolerance on material-contract BMA-access and PIPA s.10 failures) and state a conclusion: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the Chief Audit Executive — who negotiated none of the sampled contracts — sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report results to the risk committee alongside the quarterly outsourcing pack.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the risk committee.

checklist.step: Define the screening criteria that trigger a full assessment
actions: Write the high-risk trigger list into the procedure: sensitive personal information at scale, profiling or automated decisions affecting policyholders, new overseas transfers, novel technology (AI models, biometrics), matching/combining datasets, processing of vulnerable individuals' data, and any change touching a BMA-critical service.
Agree with the Chief Info Security Officer which triggers also demand the cyber threat/vulnerability leg (new internet exposure, new critical-service dependency, new data store).
Publish the screening questionnaire as a mandatory PPM intake artifact and version it with an effective date.
checklist.done: a versioned trigger list and screening questionnaire are published and embedded in PPM intake.

checklist.step: Embed the assessment gate in project intake
actions: Configure the PPM stage-gate so no initiative passes the design gate without a completed screening questionnaire, and no initiative passes the go-live gate while a DPIA/cyber assessment task is open.
Auto-create the GRC assessment task when screening answers hit a trigger.
Report monthly to the Data Protection Officer any initiative that changed scope after screening — scope drift is the classic way high-risk processing sneaks past the gate.
checklist.done: PPM gates block design and go-live on open assessment tasks and scope-drift reporting runs monthly.

checklist.step: Screen each initiative and record the outcome
actions: Complete the screening questionnaire with the Project Manager within 10 business days of intake: data categories, volumes, individuals affected, systems, vendors, transfers, and critical-service impact.
Record the outcome — full DPIA required, cyber assessment required, both, or screened out — with a two-sentence rationale.
Have the Data Protection Officer countersign every screened-out decision on a triggered questionnaire; silence is not a screening outcome.
checklist.done: every intake carries a completed questionnaire, a recorded outcome with rationale, and countersigned screen-outs.

checklist.step: Describe the processing and its necessity in the DPIA
actions: Document in the DPIA template: the processing flow end to end (collection, storage, use, disclosure, deletion), the PIPA s.6 condition of use relied on, and the link to the processing-register entry (REG-054-C25).
Write the necessity and proportionality analysis: why this data, this volume, this retention — and what less-intrusive alternative was rejected and why.
Attach the data-flow diagram from the Solutions Architect showing systems, interfaces and any overseas hop.
checklist.done: the DPIA describes the full flow, names the lawful condition, and contains a real necessity analysis with a data-flow diagram.

checklist.step: Run the cyber threat and vulnerability leg on the initiative's assets
actions: Enumerate the initiative's information assets and map them to critical insurance services as the BMA Cyber Code's risk-assessment provisions require.
Run or request an authenticated vulnerability scan of the new/changed components in Qualys/Tenable and pull the finding list by severity.
Ask the Threat Detection Engineer for the applicable threat scenarios (external attack surface, third-party compromise, insider misuse) and record which apply.
For internet-facing components, request a penetration test from the Penetration Tester and attach the report reference.
checklist.done: assets are mapped to critical services, scan results and threat scenarios are attached, and internet-facing components carry a pen-test reference.

checklist.step: Score the risks and set mitigations
actions: Score each identified privacy and cyber risk on the enterprise likelihood/impact scale in the GRC platform, before and after proposed mitigations.
Record each mitigation with a named owner and an implementation date tied to the release plan.
Flag any residual risk above appetite for the acceptance decision at approval — mitigations promised without owners are not mitigations.
checklist.done: every risk carries inherent and residual scores and every mitigation has an owner and a date.

checklist.step: Approve the assessment before go-live
actions: Review the assessment package: DPIA, cyber leg, risk scores and mitigation plan; the CISO approves the cyber conclusions, the Data Protection Officer approves the privacy conclusions.
Where residual risk exceeds appetite, take the acceptance decision to the Operational Risk Manager and record the accepting executive by name.
Record both approvals with dates in the GRC record — the PPM go-live gate reads this status.
checklist.done: both approvals are dated in the GRC record before the go-live gate opens, with any over-appetite acceptance named.

checklist.step: Consult PrivCom Bermuda where high residual privacy risk remains
actions: Where a DPIA concludes high residual risk to individuals that mitigations cannot reduce, draft a consultation note to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Bermuda describing the processing, the risk and the proposed safeguards.
Hold go-live for the affected processing until the consultation response or a documented counsel decision to proceed with enhanced safeguards.
File the consultation correspondence with the DPIA record.
checklist.done: high-residual-risk DPIAs show either a PrivCom consultation trail or a documented counsel decision with enhanced safeguards.

checklist.step: Track remediation items to closure
actions: Load every mitigation and finding into the GRC remediation module with severity-based dates: critical 30 days, high 90 days, medium 180 days.
Verify closure evidence before closing — a rescan showing the vulnerability gone, a config export, an executed contract clause — not just an owner's assertion.
Escalate items past date to the CISO weekly; extensions need the CISO's written approval with a new date.
checklist.done: all items carry severity dates, closures carry evidence, and overdue items show weekly CISO escalation.

checklist.step: Register the completed assessment
actions: Add the assessment to the DPIA/cyber-assessment register: initiative, date, outcome, residual risk, approvals, remediation status, next review trigger.
Cross-reference the processing-register entry so the two registers point at each other.
File the full package in the compliance evidence repository under the initiative name.
checklist.done: the register row exists with cross-references and the full package is filed and retrievable.

checklist.step: Re-assess on material change
actions: Define material-change triggers on each assessment: new data categories, new vendor, new jurisdiction, doubled volume, architectural change.
Subscribe to the initiative's change records in the PPM tool; when a trigger fires, reopen the assessment and re-run the affected sections.
Record 'no material change' confirmations at each annual anniversary for live high-risk processing.
checklist.done: material-change triggers are defined, fired triggers reopened assessments, and annual confirmations exist for live high-risk processing.

checklist.step: Run the annual enterprise cyber risk assessment refresh
actions: Each Q3, refresh the enterprise-wide assessment the BMA Cyber Code expects: aggregate the year's initiative assessments, the current Qualys/Tenable posture, threat-intelligence input and third-party risk into a single threats-and-vulnerabilities view over information assets and critical services.
Produce the prioritised remediation plan with owners, dates and budget asks.
Present the refreshed assessment to the board (or its risk committee) as part of the annual cyber report and minute the discussion.
checklist.done: a refreshed enterprise assessment with a prioritised remediation plan is minuted at board level in the year.

checklist.step: Catch and retrofit initiatives that bypassed the gate
actions: Quarterly, reconcile release records against the assessment register; any go-live with no screening record is a bypass.
Order a retrospective assessment within 30 days for each bypass and log the exception with root cause (intake skipped, scope drift, shadow IT).
Report bypass counts to the privacy governance committee — a rising trend means the PPM gate needs rework, not more memos.
checklist.done: quarterly reconciliations run, every bypass has a logged exception and a retrospective assessment within 30 days.

checklist.step: Report assessment-programme health to governance
actions: Report quarterly: assessments completed, screen-out rate, open remediation by severity and age, bypasses, and PrivCom consultations in flight.
Have the CISO co-present the cyber remediation position so one committee sees both legs.
Minute decisions on any systemic finding.
checklist.done: a quarterly co-presented report with minutes covers both privacy and cyber legs.

checklist.step: Retain assessment evidence
actions: Apply the 6-years-from-go-live retention label to each assessment package, approval record and remediation closure.
Verify retrieval by initiative name and by system for exam-readiness.
Hold records subject to any open incident, PrivCom or BMA inquiry.
checklist.done: packages are labelled, retrievable by initiative and system, with holds applied where required.

testing.step: Build the population of go-lives for the period
actions: Extract all initiatives that reached go-live in the period from the PPM tool.
Add production release records from the release calendar and vendor go-lives from Procurement so PPM-invisible changes surface.
Reconcile the sources and sign the combined population with counts and extract dates.
testing.done: a reconciled, dated population of go-lives exists including release-calendar and vendor additions.

testing.step: Reconcile go-lives to screening records
actions: Match every population row to a screening questionnaire in the GRC platform.
Rows with no screening record are automatic bypass exceptions — no judgement applied.
Check screening dates precede design-gate dates; retro-dated screenings are exceptions.
testing.done: every go-live is matched to a pre-dated screening or listed as a bypass exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of initiatives whose screening triggered a full assessment.
Add 15 screened-out initiatives selected at random (seeded, reproducible) to test the screening judgement itself.
Record seed, population and selection date.
testing.done: the sample covers all triggered assessments plus a reproducible screened-out selection.

testing.step: Re-perform the screening judgement on screened-out initiatives
actions: Read each sampled screened-out questionnaire and the initiative's actual scope from PPM, then reach your own trigger conclusion before reading the recorded outcome.
A screen-out you would have triggered is an exception; check whether the required DPO countersignature exists on it.
Note scope drift between screening answers and what actually shipped.
testing.done: independent screening conclusions are documented for every sampled screen-out with drift noted.

testing.step: Assess DPIA quality on the triggered sample
actions: Check each sampled DPIA contains a full processing description, a named PIPA s.6 condition, a genuine necessity analysis and a data-flow diagram — template boilerplate scores as absent.
Verify the linked processing-register entry exists and matches the DPIA's description.
Confirm risks carry inherent and residual scores and mitigations carry owners and dates.
testing.done: each sampled DPIA passes the content checks or its gaps are itemised as exceptions.

testing.step: Verify the cyber leg against scanner evidence
actions: For sampled initiatives with a cyber leg, open Qualys/Tenable and confirm a scan of the named assets ran in the assessment window and its findings match those in the assessment.
Confirm internet-facing components carry a pen-test report reference and the report exists.
Check asset-to-critical-service mapping was recorded as the BMA Cyber Code's risk-assessment provisions require.
testing.done: scanner and pen-test evidence corroborates each sampled cyber assessment and mappings are recorded.

testing.step: Verify approvals pre-date go-live
actions: Compare the CISO and DPO approval dates in the GRC record to the actual production go-live date from the release calendar.
Any approval dated after go-live, or any go-live with the assessment task still open, is an exception.
For over-appetite acceptances, confirm the accepting executive is named and the acceptance pre-dates go-live.
testing.done: every sampled go-live shows both approvals dated before release, with acceptances properly named.

testing.step: Recompute remediation timeliness
actions: For all remediation items on sampled assessments, recompute days-open against the severity SLA (critical 30, high 90, medium 180).
Check closed items carry closure evidence (rescan, config export) rather than assertion-only closure.
List items past SLA without a written CISO extension as exceptions.
testing.done: SLA maths is recomputed for every item and evidence-free closures or unextended overdue items are listed.

testing.step: Confirm the annual enterprise refresh occurred
actions: Retrieve the enterprise cyber risk assessment and confirm it was refreshed within the last 12 months.
Trace it to the board or risk-committee minutes showing presentation and discussion.
Verify the remediation plan carries owners, dates and current status.
testing.done: a ≤12-month-old enterprise assessment traces to committee minutes with a live remediation plan.

testing.step: Log exceptions, conclude and obtain independent sign-off
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception (bypass, wrong screen-out, late approval, evidence-free closure) with root cause, owner and remediation date.
Compute the fail rate against the zero-bypass threshold and write the conclusion: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the Chief Audit Executive — segregated from all sampled assessments — sign the workpaper, file it in the evidence repository and report to the privacy governance committee and the CISO.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with logged exceptions and a stated conclusion is filed and reported to both governance owners.

checklist.step: Maintain the notification runbook and severity matrix
actions: Keep the runbook current: severity levels, the BMA materiality decision tree (impact on critical operations, policyholder data, availability duration), the PIPA adverse-effect test, and named contact routes for the BMA supervisory team and PrivCom Bermuda.

Store pre-approved notification templates for the BMA initial notice, the BMA follow-up report, the PrivCom notice and the individual notice, each cleared in advance by Regulatory Counsel and Privacy Counsel.
Re-approve the runbook annually with the CISO, Privacy Officer and Regulatory Counsel, and after every material incident's lessons-learned.
checklist.done: a current runbook with pre-cleared templates and named regulator contact routes carries this year's approval.

checklist.step: Configure detection and escalation so incidents reach the clock-owners fast
actions: Maintain Splunk correlation searches for the notification-relevant scenarios: data exfiltration indicators, ransomware behaviour, unauthorised access to policy/claims data stores, and critical-service outages.
Set the SOAR playbook to open an ITSM security incident automatically at high severity and page the on-call Incident Response Lead within 15 minutes.
Test the paging path monthly and log the test in the ticketing system.
checklist.done: correlation searches cover the notification scenarios and the monthly paging test passes.

checklist.step: Triage and classify every incident on intake
actions: Within 4 hours of ticket creation, assign severity from the matrix and record affected systems, services and suspected data categories.
Flag on the ticket two booleans that drive everything downstream: 'potential material cyber event (BMA)' and 'potential personal-information breach (PIPA)'.
Open the incident bridge and assign roles per the runbook for severity 1-2 incidents.
checklist.done: every incident ticket carries severity, both notification flags and role assignments within 4 hours.

checklist.step: Scope the incident forensically
actions: Acquire and preserve evidence (disk/memory images, log exports with hashes) before remediation destroys it, logging chain of custody on the ticket.

Determine what data was accessed or exfiltrated: identify the tables/files touched, count affected individuals, and classify the personal-information categories against the processing register (REG-054-C25).
Determine operational impact: which critical insurance services were degraded, for how long, and whether policyholder-facing functions failed.
Write the scoping note the materiality decision will cite — dates, counts, categories, services.
checklist.done: a chain-of-custody evidence set and a scoping note with counts, categories and service impact exist on the ticket.

checklist.step: Make and date the BMA materiality determination
actions: Convene the CISO, Incident Response Lead and Regulatory Counsel and run the materiality decision tree against the scoping note: does the event materially affect critical operations, policyholder data or the insurer's risk profile as the BMA Cyber Code contemplates.
Record the determination — material or not material — with reasoning and, critically, the determination date and time on the ticket: this timestamp starts the 14-day BMA clock.
Re-run the determination whenever forensics changes the facts; a 'not material' call is provisional until incident closure.
checklist.done: a dated, reasoned materiality determination sits on the ticket and re-determinations are logged when facts change.

checklist.step: Send the BMA initial notification within 14 days
actions: For material events, complete the pre-cleared BMA initial-notification template: event description, detection date, affected services and data, containment status, and interim contact.
Submit to the BMA supervisory contact through the established channel no later than 14 days after the materiality determination date — target day 7 to keep margin.
Log the submission timestamp and the BMA acknowledgement on the incident ticket and file the letter in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the initial notification is filed with a submission timestamp on or before day 14 and the acknowledgement is logged.

checklist.step: Run the PIPA adverse-effect assessment in parallel
actions: Where personal information was involved, assess against PIPA s.14: is the breach of security likely to adversely affect the individuals concerned — considering data sensitivity, exposure, and misuse potential.
Record the assessment with reasoning and date on the ticket; this is a separate judgement from BMA materiality and one does not imply the other.
Have Privacy Counsel countersign every 'no adverse effect' conclusion.
checklist.done: a dated, countersigned PIPA adverse-effect assessment exists for every incident touching personal information.

checklist.step: Notify the Privacy Commissioner without undue delay
actions: For breaches meeting the adverse-effect test, complete the PrivCom notification: nature of the breach, categories and approximate number of individuals, likely consequences, and measures taken.

Submit to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Bermuda via its published notification route as soon as the facts support a coherent notice — do not hold for the full forensic report; supplement later.
Log the submission timestamp and any PrivCom case reference on the ticket.
checklist.done: the PrivCom notice is submitted without undue delay with its timestamp and case reference logged.

checklist.step: Notify affected individuals
actions: Draft the individual notice from the pre-cleared template: what happened, what data, what the company is doing, and concrete self-protection steps; have the Communications Specialist plain-language it and Privacy Counsel clear it.
Choose the delivery channel per the policyholder contact data (letter, secure portal message, email) and dispatch to the affected population identified in the forensic scoping.
Stand up the response route (dedicated line or mailbox via the Contact Center Ops Manager) before notices land.
Retain the dispatch list and delivery receipts against the ticket.
checklist.done: cleared notices are dispatched to the full affected population with dispatch lists and receipts retained.

checklist.step: File the BMA follow-up report within 14 days of the initial notification
actions: Complete the follow-up template: root cause, full impact assessment, remediation performed and planned, and control improvements.
Submit within 14 days of the initial notification date — the ticket's day-7 and day-12 tasks track this second clock.
Answer any further BMA questions within the timeframe the BMA sets, logging each exchange on the ticket.
checklist.done: the follow-up report is filed within its 14-day window and all BMA exchanges are logged.

checklist.step: Keep the notification clock evidence airtight
actions: Maintain on the ticket a single chronology table: detection, triage, scoping note, materiality determination, BMA initial, PrivCom notice, individual dispatch, BMA follow-up — each with date-time and actor.
Verify the SOAR-created day-7/day-12 tasks were completed or consciously closed, never silently expired.
Lock the chronology at incident closure so it cannot be edited after the fact.
checklist.done: a locked chronology with all timestamps and actors exists on every notifiable incident.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review and feed the runbook
actions: Within 20 business days of closure, hold the post-incident review: detection speed, decision quality, clock performance, template fitness.
Log improvement actions with owners and dates; route control gaps into the cyber risk assessment (REG-054-C27) remediation plan.
Update the runbook and templates where the incident exposed friction.
checklist.done: a post-incident review with owned actions exists and runbook updates are versioned.

checklist.step: Exercise the notification path annually even without incidents
actions: Run a tabletop annually simulating a material breach with personal information: participants must produce a mock materiality determination, a drafted BMA notice and a drafted PrivCom notice against the real clocks.
Include the Privacy Officer, Regulatory Counsel and Communications Specialist so the cross-functional handoffs are tested, not just the SOC.
Record the exercise date, findings and fixes in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: an annual tabletop produced mock notices against the clocks with recorded findings and fixes.

checklist.step: Report notification performance to governance
actions: Report quarterly to the risk committee: incident counts by severity, notifiable events, clock performance against the 14-day windows, and open improvement actions.
Report material incidents to the board per the Cyber Code's governance expectations, with the notification chronology attached.
Minute decisions and any risk acceptance.
checklist.done: quarterly committee reporting covers clock performance and material incidents reached the board with chronologies.

checklist.step: Retain incident and notification evidence
actions: File each incident package — ticket export, forensic report, determinations, notices, receipts, post-incident review — under the incident ID with the 6-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by incident ID, date and regulator notified.
Apply litigation/inquiry holds where PrivCom, the BMA or claimants remain active.
checklist.done: incident packages are filed, labelled for 6-year retention and retrievable by ID, date and regulator.

testing.step: Build the incident population
actions: Extract every security incident ticket opened in the review period with severity, flags, and status.
Extract Splunk high-severity alert counts for the same period as an independent completeness check.
Record both counts and extract dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: a dated incident population with an independent SIEM count exists.

testing.step: Reconcile SIEM alerts to tickets
actions: Sample 20 high-severity Splunk alerts and trace each to an incident ticket or a documented triage dismissal.
Alerts with no ticket and no dismissal are completeness exceptions — incidents may have been worked over chat and never notified.
Check auto-ticketing playbook logs for gaps or failures in the period.
testing.done: sampled alerts trace to tickets or dismissals and playbook gaps are listed.

testing.step: Draw the incident sample
actions: Take 100% of incidents flagged material (BMA) or personal-information breach (PIPA), and 100% of severity-1/2 incidents regardless of flags.
Add 10 randomly selected (seeded, reproducible) lower-severity incidents to test under-flagging.
Record seed, population and selection date.
testing.done: the sample covers every flagged and high-severity incident plus a reproducible low-severity selection.

testing.step: Re-perform the materiality and adverse-effect judgements
actions: For each sampled incident, read the forensic scoping note and reach your own BMA-materiality and PIPA adverse-effect conclusions before reading the recorded ones.
A 'not material' or 'no adverse effect' call you would overturn is an exception with immediate CISO escalation — it may mean an unnotified notifiable event.
Check 'no adverse effect' conclusions carry the Privacy Counsel countersignature.
testing.done: independent determinations are documented per sampled incident and overturned calls are escalated.

testing.step: Recompute every notification clock
actions: From each chronology, recompute: materiality-determination date + 14 days vs BMA initial-notification timestamp; initial-notification date + 14 days vs follow-up timestamp.
For PIPA notices, assess 'without undue delay' — days from adverse-effect confirmation to PrivCom submission — and flag anything over 5 business days without documented justification.
Any blown window is a fail regardless of by how little.
testing.done: all clocks are recomputed with day counts in the workpaper and every blown window is flagged.

testing.step: Trace notifications to filed evidence and identifiers
actions: Retrieve each BMA letter and acknowledgement, each PrivCom notice and case reference, from the evidence repository and match content to the incident facts.
Verify individual-notice dispatch lists reconcile to the forensically determined affected population — a dispatch list smaller than the affected count is an exception.
Check delivery receipts or returned-mail handling exist for individual notices.
testing.done: every notification traces to filed evidence with identifiers, and dispatch lists reconcile to affected counts.

testing.step: Verify chronology integrity
actions: Compare chronology timestamps to underlying system timestamps (SIEM alert time, ticket audit trail, email send times) for each sampled incident.
Flag chronology entries with no corroborating system timestamp as evidence-integrity exceptions.
Confirm chronologies were locked at closure and show no post-closure edits.
testing.done: chronology entries corroborate against system timestamps and locks show no post-closure edits.

testing.step: Verify the annual tabletop ran and paging works
actions: Retrieve the tabletop record and confirm it produced mock determinations and drafted notices against the real clocks within the last 12 months.
Check the monthly paging-path tests ran and failures were fixed.
Confirm cross-functional participants (Privacy, Legal, Communications) attended, not just the SOC.
testing.done: a ≤12-month-old tabletop with cross-functional attendance and passing paging tests is evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date

For unnotified events and blown windows, open a corrective-disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel — deciding whether to notify the BMA or PrivCom now, late, is a legal call that must be made and documented.
Assign root cause, owner and remediation date on each issue.
testing.done: every exception is logged and every notification failure carries a documented corrective-disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the zero-tolerance threshold: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, with the clock recomputation table attached.
Have the Chief Audit Executive — outside the incident command chain for all sampled incidents — sign the workpaper.
File it in the compliance evidence repository and report to the risk committee with the CISO and Privacy Officer present.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and clock table is filed and reported to the risk committee.
