checklist.step: Define the role-based curriculum map
actions: Map the all-staff core module topics: PIPA conditions of use, individuals' rights, safeguards and clean-desk practice, breach recognition and the internal reporting route, and the Code's fair-treatment-of-policyholders expectations.

Define enhanced modules per role family: claims handlers (fair claims handling, sensitive health data), sales/distribution (fair sales conduct, disclosures), contact-center (identity verification, call-recording notices), underwriting (data minimisation).
Record the curriculum map with module owners and versions in the procedure document.
checklist.done: a versioned curriculum map covers core and role-based modules with named owners.

checklist.step: Refresh course content before each annual campaign
actions: Update the modules with the year's regulatory changes supplied by Privacy Counsel (PIPA guidance, PrivCom decisions, BMA Code updates) and with anonymised lessons from the year's incidents and complaints.
Rebuild the assessment bank so pass-marks test application, not recall — scenario questions drawn from real (anonymised) cases.
Route the refreshed content to the Privacy Officer and Privacy Counsel for sign-off, and version it in the LMS by 15 August.
checklist.done: refreshed, counsel-signed content is versioned in the LMS before 15 August.

checklist.step: Load courses and assignment rules into the LMS
actions: Publish the course versions in Cornerstone and build assignment rules keyed to HRIS job-family codes so each person receives core plus their role modules.
Set the pass mark at 80%, two retakes then instructor referral, and completion certificates on.
Configure the reminder cadence (assignment, T-14, T-7, T-1) and the manager-copy on overdue notices.
Dry-run assignment on a pilot group of 20 and fix mis-mappings before the campaign opens.
checklist.done: courses, rules, pass-marks and reminders are configured and the pilot dry-run assigned correctly.

checklist.step: Wire the HRIS joiner/mover/leaver feed
actions: Confirm the nightly HRIS-to-LMS feed carries hires, transfers and terminations with job-family codes, and that contractors with system access are included via the contingent-worker records.
Set new hires to auto-receive the core module on day 1 with a 30-day due date from start date.
On transfer into a role family with an enhanced module, auto-assign it with a 30-day due date.
Monitor the feed error queue weekly and clear failures with the Systems Administrator.
checklist.done: the nightly feed assigns joiners and movers automatically with 30-day due dates and the error queue is worked weekly.

checklist.step: Open and run the annual campaign
actions: Open the campaign to the full HRIS-derived population on 1 September with a 31 October close.
Publish a launch communication from the Privacy Officer explaining why the training exists — cite the Code's fair-treatment duty and PIPA, not just 'mandatory training'.
Track completion weekly by department in the LMS dashboard and send the standings to department heads each Friday.
checklist.done: the campaign opened on schedule to the full population and weekly standings go to department heads.

checklist.step: Chase and escalate non-completion
actions: Let the LMS reminders run their cadence; at T-7 days send managers their outstanding lists directly.
At campaign close, hand the non-completer list to HR Business Partners for the escalation ladder: manager conversation within 5 business days, then written notice.
At close + 30 days, refer persistent non-completers to the Privacy Officer for the access-restriction decision with the Access Management route via IAM.
checklist.done: the escalation ladder ran on schedule and persistent non-completers reached the access-restriction decision point.

checklist.step: Enforce the new-hire 30-day SLA year-round
actions: Review the monthly LMS report of hires past day 25 without completion and prompt their managers same-week.
Treat completion as an onboarding-checklist gate: probation reviews must confirm the training is done.
Report the monthly SLA percentage to the Privacy Officer with reasons for misses.
checklist.done: monthly SLA reporting runs and day-25 prompts fire before hires breach the 30-day window.

checklist.step: Deliver enhanced modules to high-risk role families
actions: Run the claims, sales/distribution and contact-center enhanced modules as instructor-led or virtual sessions where scenario discussion matters more than e-learning.
Record attendance in the LMS against the enhanced-module assignment so completion reporting is one system.
Collect scenario-question performance to feed the next content refresh — persistent wrong answers mark unclear procedure, not stupid staff.
checklist.done: enhanced modules ran with LMS-recorded attendance and question-performance data fed back to the designer.

checklist.step: Apply the pass-mark and retake rules
actions: Verify the LMS enforces the 80% pass-mark and the two-retake limit before instructor referral.
Route third-failure cases to the Trainer for a coached session and a supervised reassessment.
Record final outcomes so no one is marked complete on a failed assessment.
checklist.done: pass-mark enforcement is verified and every third-failure case shows a coached path to a genuine pass.

checklist.step: Update content mid-year on regulatory change
actions: Monitor PIPA guidance, PrivCom publications and BMA Code updates; where a change affects front-line handling, commission a micro-module or bulletin rather than waiting for the annual refresh.
Have the Learning & Development Specialist push the micro-module to affected role families with a 30-day due date.
Log the trigger, content and assignment in the curriculum change record.
checklist.done: mid-year regulatory changes produced targeted micro-modules with 30-day assignments and a logged trail.

checklist.step: Capture acknowledgements of the privacy and conduct policies
actions: Attach the policy-acknowledgement step to the core module completion: each person attests they have read the privacy policy and code-of-conduct summary.
Store attestation timestamps with the completion record.
Reconcile attestation counts to completion counts after the campaign and chase gaps.
checklist.done: attestations are captured with completions and the two counts reconcile.

checklist.step: Report campaign results to governance
actions: Report to the privacy governance committee within 30 days of campaign close: completion % by department, new-hire SLA, assessment performance, escalations and access restrictions.
Include training completion in the annual Code-of-Conduct compliance assessment to the board (with REG-054-C30).
Minute decisions on departments below threshold.
checklist.done: a minuted post-campaign report exists and training results feed the annual board assessment.

checklist.step: Run the annual effectiveness review
actions: Correlate training data with outcomes: breach near-miss reports (a healthy increase suggests awareness), complaint themes, and incident root causes citing human error.
Interview a sample of claims and contact-center staff on what they would actually do with a suspected breach — the runbook answer, not the course answer.
Feed findings into the next curriculum refresh with documented changes.
checklist.done: an effectiveness review with outcome correlation and staff interviews produced documented curriculum changes.

checklist.step: Log and disposition training exceptions
actions: Log each post-close non-completer and each new-hire SLA breach as a GRC exception with the escalation outcome.
Record access-restriction decisions and their lift dates for persistent non-completers.
Close exceptions only on evidenced completion or documented departure.
checklist.done: every exception carries an outcome and closes only on evidenced completion or departure.

checklist.step: Retain training evidence
actions: Archive campaign reports, curriculum versions, completion and attestation records with the 6-year retention label.
Verify per-person retrieval works for exam requests — by name, department and campaign year.
Preserve records of leavers, whose completion history may be needed in later investigations.
checklist.done: training evidence is archived, labelled for 6 years and retrievable per person including leavers.

testing.step: Build the workforce population
actions: Extract from the HRIS all active employees and contingent workers during the campaign window with start dates, job-family codes and departments.
Extract the LMS campaign assignment list for the same window.
Record both counts and extract dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: dated HRIS and LMS populations with counts exist in the workpaper.

testing.step: Reconcile HRIS headcount to LMS assignments
actions: Match every HRIS person to an LMS assignment; unassigned actives are completeness exceptions — the feed or the assignment rules missed them.
Match every LMS assignment to an HRIS record; orphan assignments suggest leavers not deactivated.
Verify contractors with system access appear in both — the classic gap population.
testing.done: the two populations reconcile with every difference dispositioned, contractors included.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of staff in sensitive-data roles (claims, contact-center, underwriting, HR) flagged via job-family codes.
Add 25 randomly selected (seeded, reproducible) staff from the remainder and all hires from two sampled months for the SLA test.
Record seed, population and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering sensitive roles, general staff and new hires is drawn.

testing.step: Verify completion evidence for each sampled person
actions: Open each sampled person's LMS transcript and verify: correct course version, completion timestamp inside the campaign window, assessment score ≥80%, and the policy attestation timestamp.
Check role-family staff completed their enhanced module, not just core.
A completion recorded without a passing score, or against a superseded course version, is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled transcript shows version, timestamp, passing score and attestation, with enhanced modules where required.

testing.step: Recompute the new-hire 30-day SLA
actions: For each sampled hire, compute completion date minus HRIS start date and compare to 30 days.
Compute the population SLA rate for the two sampled months and compare to the ≥95% threshold.
Check day-25 manager prompts fired for late completers.
testing.done: per-hire day counts and the monthly SLA rate are recomputed with prompt evidence checked.

testing.step: Verify curriculum content covers the required topics
actions: Walk the current core module against the topic map: PIPA conditions of use, individuals' rights, safeguards, breach reporting route, and Code fair-treatment duties — confirm each is actually taught, not just listed.
Confirm the year's refresh incorporated the regulatory changes Privacy Counsel logged and carries counsel sign-off.
Check assessment questions test scenarios, and that the breach-reporting route taught matches the current runbook (REG-054-C28).
testing.done: the live content demonstrably covers every mapped topic, matches current procedures and carries counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Test the escalation ladder on non-completers
actions: Take the post-close non-completer list and trace 10 cases through the ladder: manager conversation, written notice, Privacy Officer referral, access-restriction decision.
Check each step's timestamps against the ladder's day counts.
Confirm restrictions were actually applied in the IAM platform for cases that reached that step, and lifted on completion.
testing.done: traced cases show the ladder ran on time and IAM restrictions match the decisions.

testing.step: Recompute the campaign completion rate
actions: Recompute completion % at campaign close and at close + 30 days from raw LMS data, by department.
Compare to the reported figures in the governance pack; differences beyond rounding are reporting-integrity exceptions.
Compare against the ≥98% and 100% thresholds.
testing.done: independently recomputed rates match the reported figures and are assessed against thresholds.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception: unassigned staff, failed-score completions, SLA breaches, ladder failures, reporting mismatches.
Assign root cause (feed gap, rule mis-mapping, manager inaction) and a named owner with a date.
Flag any sensitive-data-role individual without current training for immediate manager action, not next campaign.
testing.done: every exception is logged with cause, owner and date, and sensitive-role gaps get immediate action.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds: effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, with the reconciliation and SLA tables attached.
Have the Chief Audit Executive — who did not administer the campaign — sign the workpaper.
File it in the compliance evidence repository and report to the privacy governance committee alongside the Privacy Officer's campaign report.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the privacy governance committee.

checklist.step: Build and maintain the Code-mapped procedure inventory
actions: List every conduct area from the Code — product design and disclosure, marketing and sales, underwriting fairness, claims handling, complaints, vulnerable customers, conflicts of interest — as inventory rows in the GRC platform.
Map each row to the procedure document(s) that implement it, with the repository link, version, owner and review-by date.
Flag any Code area with no mapped procedure as an immediate gap with a drafting owner and a 60-day date.
Re-walk the mapping whenever the BMA revises the Code.
checklist.done: every Code conduct area maps to a versioned, owned procedure or carries a dated gap action.

checklist.step: Assign and confirm procedure owners annually
actions: Name one accountable owner per procedure — a role, and a person filling it — and record both in the inventory.
Re-confirm ownership each January and on every reorganisation; orphaned procedures reassign within 10 business days.
Brief new owners on their review and breach-reporting duties at handover.
checklist.done: every procedure names a current owner, re-confirmed this year, with no orphan lasting past 10 business days.

checklist.step: Run the annual review cycle on every procedure
actions: Verify GRC review tasks generate at T-60 days before each procedure's review-by date and land on the owner's queue.
Track completions weekly; chase owners at T-30 and escalate overdue reviews to the Head of Compliance at T+5 days.
Record each completed review with the reviewer, date, and the change summary (or an explicit 'no change required' with reasons).
checklist.done: every procedure shows a review within 12 months, or an escalated overdue record — none silently lapse.

checklist.step: Update procedures for regulatory and business change
actions: Monitor BMA notices, Code revisions, guidance and enforcement outcomes; log each item with an impact call against the inventory within 10 business days of publication.
Commission procedure updates for impacted areas with a completion date proportionate to the change's effective date.
Feed conduct-metric findings (REG-054-C32) and complaint root causes into the same update pipeline — procedures that ignore live failure data are decorative.
checklist.done: every logged regulatory change carries an impact call and impacted procedures show dated updates.

checklist.step: Approve procedure changes through the workflow
actions: Route every new or changed procedure through the approval workflow: owner drafts, Compliance Manager reviews, Head of Compliance approves; claims and sales procedures also get Legal Counsel review.
Reject drafts that describe aspiration rather than executable steps — a procedure a new joiner cannot follow fails the Code's purpose.
Publish approved versions to the repository with effective dates and archive superseded versions.
checklist.done: every live procedure carries a complete approval trail and superseded versions are archived, not deleted.

checklist.step: Communicate procedure changes to affected staff
actions: On each publication, notify the affected role families with a summary of what changed and from when, via the established channel.
For material changes to claims or sales conduct, commission a micro-training through the Learning & Development Specialist (links to REG-054-C29).
Record the communication date and audience on the procedure's inventory row.
checklist.done: every published change shows a dated communication to its audience, with training where material.

checklist.step: Operate the compliance function's monitoring per Code s.5/s.6
actions: Maintain the annual compliance monitoring plan covering the conduct areas, risk-weighted by complaint volumes, metric breaches and prior findings.
Execute the plan's reviews — file checks in claims and new business, sales-call sampling, disclosure reviews — and record results in the GRC platform.
Report monitoring outcomes quarterly to the conduct/risk committee with trends and actions.
checklist.done: a risk-weighted monitoring plan exists, its reviews are executed and recorded, and outcomes reach the committee quarterly.

checklist.step: Define and apply the breach materiality criteria
actions: Document the materiality test for Code breaches: policyholder harm scale, systemic vs isolated, duration, financial impact, and whether the failure undermines the BMA's view of sound and prudent conduct.
Assess every logged breach against the test within 10 business days of identification, recording the rationale, not just the label.
Route every 'material' assessment — and every borderline call — to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel the same week.
checklist.done: every breach carries a dated, reasoned materiality assessment within 10 business days, with material and borderline calls escalated.

checklist.step: Self-report material failures to the BMA
actions: For each breach confirmed material, draft the BMA report: the failure, affected policyholders, root cause, remediation underway and prevention measures — candour calibrated with the General Counsel.
Submit to the BMA supervisory contact promptly on determination — target within 10 business days — and log the submission date and any BMA response on the breach record.
Track BMA follow-up questions to closure within whatever timeframe the BMA sets.
checklist.done: every material breach shows a BMA report within the target window and follow-ups tracked to closure.

checklist.step: Drive breach remediation to closure
actions: Attach to each breach a remediation plan with actions, owners and dates, including policyholder redress where harm occurred.
Verify closure evidence — the corrected procedure, the redress payment run, the retrained team — before closing the record.
Report open material remediations to the conduct/risk committee until closed.
checklist.done: every breach carries an owned remediation plan and closes only on verified evidence.

checklist.step: Track procedure exceptions and waivers
actions: Log every approved deviation from a conduct procedure (e.g. a claims-handling exception in a catastrophe surge) with scope, expiry and approver.
Review open waivers monthly and close expired ones — perpetual waivers are unwritten procedure changes and must either die or become the procedure.
Include waiver counts in the quarterly committee pack.
checklist.done: every deviation is logged with expiry and approver, and no waiver survives its expiry unreviewed.

checklist.step: Report the conduct-programme position to the board
actions: Present quarterly to the conduct/risk committee: inventory health, overdue reviews, breach register with materiality mix, self-reports made, and remediation status.
Produce the annual Code-of-Conduct compliance assessment for the board, integrating training (REG-054-C29), metrics (REG-054-C32) and outsourcing (REG-054-C26) inputs.
Minute board challenge and decisions.
checklist.done: quarterly packs and a minuted annual board assessment cover the full conduct programme.

checklist.step: Prepare the BMA-facing evidence pack
actions: Maintain the standing pack: Code-mapped inventory export, current procedure versions, breach register summary and self-report log, refreshed quarterly.
Dry-run the 5-business-day production drill annually against a simulated BMA conduct-review request.
Fix assembly friction found in the drill and record the result.
checklist.done: a ≤1-quarter-old evidence pack exists and the annual production drill met the 5-day target.

checklist.step: Handle whistleblowing and staff-reported conduct concerns
actions: Operate the confidential reporting channel and triage each report for Code relevance within 5 business days.
Route substantiated conduct failures into the breach register for materiality assessment — staff reports are a primary detection source the BMA expects to work.
Report channel volumes and outcomes (anonymised) to the conduct/risk committee quarterly.
checklist.done: staff reports are triaged within 5 days, substantiated ones enter the breach register, and volumes reach the committee.

checklist.step: Retain conduct-programme evidence
actions: Retain procedure versions, review records, breach assessments and BMA correspondence 6 years with the retention label applied.
Verify retrieval by Code section, procedure name and breach ID.
Apply holds where BMA engagement or policyholder litigation is open.
checklist.done: conduct evidence is labelled, retrievable by Code section and breach ID, with holds applied where required.

testing.step: Build the population from the inventory and breach register
actions: Extract the full procedure inventory with owners, versions and review dates, and the full breach/exception register for the period.
Extract the document repository's list of live conduct procedures as an independent source.
Record counts and extract dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: dated inventory, register and repository extracts with counts exist.

testing.step: Reconcile the inventory to the Code and the repository
actions: Walk the Code's conduct provisions section by section and confirm each maps to an inventory row — an unmapped Code area is a completeness exception.
Match inventory rows to live repository documents; rows pointing at missing or draft-status documents are exceptions.
List repository conduct procedures absent from the inventory as shadow-procedure findings.
testing.done: Code sections, inventory rows and repository documents reconcile three ways with differences dispositioned.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of breaches assessed material or borderline, and 100% of procedures past their review-by date at any point in the year.
Add 12 randomly selected (seeded, reproducible) procedures and 10 random non-material breaches.
Record seed, population and selection date.
testing.done: the sample covers all material/borderline breaches and overdue procedures plus reproducible random selections.

testing.step: Verify review currency and approval trails on sampled procedures
actions: For each sampled procedure, check the last review date is within 12 months and the approval trail (owner, Compliance Manager, Head of Compliance, Legal where required) is complete on the live version.
Verify 'no change required' reviews carry reasons rather than a bare tick.
Check superseded versions were archived and the effective dates chain without gaps.
testing.done: each sampled procedure shows a ≤12-month review, a complete approval trail and a gapless version chain.

testing.step: Assess procedure executability
actions: For 5 sampled procedures, have an operational staff member outside compliance walk through the written steps against the live system screens.
Log steps that no longer match the system or that require unwritten tribal knowledge as quality exceptions.
Verify the communicated-change records reached the walkers' teams for recent updates.
testing.done: walked procedures either execute as written or their divergences are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform materiality assessments on sampled breaches
actions: Read each sampled breach's facts and apply the materiality test independently before reading the recorded assessment.
A 'not material' call you would overturn is an exception with immediate Head of Compliance escalation — it may mean an unreported reportable failure.
Check assessments were completed within 10 business days of identification.
testing.done: independent materiality conclusions are documented and overturned or late assessments are escalated.

testing.step: Trace material breaches to BMA self-reports
actions: For every material breach, retrieve the BMA report and compute days from materiality determination to submission against the 10-business-day target.
Verify the report content matches the breach record — sanitised reports that omit known facts are exceptions with General Counsel referral.
Confirm BMA follow-up questions were answered within the timeframes the BMA set.
testing.done: every material breach traces to a timely, factually complete BMA report with closed follow-ups.

testing.step: Verify remediation closure evidence
actions: For each sampled closed breach, retrieve the closure evidence: corrected procedure version, redress run, retraining records.
Reopen (as exceptions) closures resting on assertions without artifacts.
Check redress reached the affected policyholders by tracing a payment sample to the billing platform.
testing.done: sampled closures carry real artifacts and redress traces to actual payments.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception: unmapped Code area, stale procedure, overturned materiality call, late or missing self-report, assertion-only closure.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a date.
Route any unreported reportable failure to Regulatory Counsel for a corrective self-report decision, documented either way.
testing.done: every exception is logged and unreported failures carry a documented corrective-disclosure decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds (no unmapped Code area, no unreported material breach): effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the Chief Audit Executive — owner of no sampled procedure — sign the workpaper.
File it in the compliance evidence repository and present to the conduct/risk committee with the Head of Compliance in attendance.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and presented to the conduct/risk committee.

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: MCAS submissions due April 30 for the prior calendar data year (life/annuity and most lines; state variations logged per the data-call letters); MCAS user registrations verified by March 1; internal data lock March 31

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar milestones at T-90 (scope confirmed), T-60 (data extracted), T-30 (validation clean), T-14 (attestation) and T-7 days before April 30, with alerts to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submission confirmations, filed data sets, reconciliation workpapers and attestation records retained 7 years in the compliance evidence repository under Reporting/MCAS

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any late submission, missed state/line, or post-filing correction is logged with root cause, the state's response, and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every refiling and every late-filing remediation; the Head of Compliance countersigns where a state issues an inquiry or penalty

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The scope matrix of writing company × state × line for the data year (derived from Schedule T premiums vs state thresholds) and all MCAS submissions actually made for that year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any required state/line combination with no timely submission is a fail; any sampled data element deviating from source-system recomputation beyond 1% is a fail; ≥1 missed filing escalates to the Head of Compliance

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or submitted any tested MCAS filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS test workpaper (scope matrix, submission trace, element recomputations, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Reporting/MCAS/Testing

checklist.step: Determine the filing scope for the data year
actions: Each January, pull the NAIC MCAS participation chart and the states' data-call letters for the lines the group writes.
Extract prior-year written premium by state and line from the Annual Statement Schedule T for each US-admitted writing company.
Apply each state's premium threshold (commonly $50,000 per line) to build the scope matrix: company × state × line = filing required or not, with the threshold maths recorded per cell.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager countersign the matrix, and diarise re-checks for states newly adopting MCAS lines this year.
checklist.done: a countersigned scope matrix with per-cell threshold maths exists by 31 January.

checklist.step: Verify MCAS portal access and user registrations
actions: Log in to the NAIC MCAS portal by March 1 and verify the company's registrations cover every in-scope company and line, under the correct NAIC company codes.
Confirm the MCAS Administrator and preparer accounts are current — reassign any held by leavers via the NAIC's account management.
Record the verified user list and company-code mapping in the filing workpaper.
checklist.done: portal access is verified by March 1 for every in-scope company with a recorded user and code mapping.

checklist.step: Map data elements to the current MCAS blanks
actions: Download the data year's MCAS blanks and definitions for each line from the NAIC MCAS page and diff them against last year's — the NAIC changes definitions and adds interrogatories most years.

Update the element-mapping document: each MCAS field (claims opened/closed, claims closed with/without payment by duration buckets, lawsuits opened/closed, complaints, policies issued/in-force/cancelled, replacements for life/annuity) mapped to its source system, table and filter logic.
Route mapping changes to the Data Analyst for extract-code updates and to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for approval.
checklist.done: an approved mapping document reflecting the current-year blanks exists with every field sourced.

checklist.step: Extract source data from the admin and claims platforms
actions: Run the approved extract queries against the warehouse tables fed by the policy admin and claims platforms for the calendar data year, by company, state and line.

Apply the MCAS definitions exactly — e.g. claim duration measured from report date to final payment date, lawsuits counted by claimant per the line's definitions — not internal operational definitions.
Freeze the extract by March 31 with row counts, query versions and run dates logged.
Deliver the extract to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst with a data dictionary.
checklist.done: a frozen March 31 extract with logged counts, versions and MCAS-definition alignment is delivered.

checklist.step: Reconcile extracted premiums to Schedule T
actions: Compare extracted written premium by company/state/line to the filed Annual Statement Schedule T figures.
Investigate any variance above 1% to a documented cause (intercompany reinsurance, line mapping, timing) and record the explanation.
Sign the reconciliation — MCAS figures a state cannot tie to the Annual Statement are the fastest route to an examiner letter.
checklist.done: a signed premium reconciliation exists with every >1% variance explained.

checklist.step: Compute the MCAS interrogatory values and ratios
actions: Populate the per-state workbooks from the frozen extract, computing each blank's values and the derived ratios the states watch (e.g. claims closed without payment ratio, median days to final payment, complaint ratios, replacement ratios for life/annuity).
Run the NAIC's published validation rules over each workbook and clear every error and explainable warning.
Version the workbooks in the filing folder with formulas intact — no pasted values.
checklist.done: per-state workbooks compute clean against NAIC validations with formulas intact.

checklist.step: Review results against prior year and benchmarks
actions: Compare each state/line's key ratios to prior year and to the NAIC's published MCAS scorecard averages; flag movements beyond 20% relative for explanation.
Obtain written explanations from the Claims Director / Manager or UW Operations Manager for flagged movements — states ask about outliers, and the answer must exist before filing.
Log the review outcomes and explanations in the filing workpaper for the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: flagged ratio movements carry written business explanations logged before submission.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation
actions: Present the final per-state figures, reconciliation and outlier explanations to the attesting officer per the MCAS requirement.
Capture the attestation in the portal (or the state's prescribed form) by the T-14 milestone, naming the officer and date.
File the attestation record with the filing workpaper.
checklist.done: a named, dated officer attestation exists for every filing by T-14.

checklist.step: Submit each filing in the MCAS portal by April 30
actions: In the NAIC MCAS portal, select the company and data year, enter or upload each state/line's data, and re-run the portal's validation before submitting.
Submit every required state/line by April 30 — target April 23 to keep a week's margin for portal issues.
Save the per-filing submission confirmation (timestamp and filing ID) to the compliance evidence repository the same day.
Tick off each scope-matrix cell as its confirmation lands; the matrix must show 100% before the deadline.
checklist.done: every scope-matrix cell shows a portal confirmation timestamped on or before April 30.

checklist.step: Track the filing calendar and escalate slippage
actions: Maintain the milestone calendar (T-90 scope, T-60 extract, T-30 validation, T-14 attestation, T-7 pre-deadline check) with alerts to the analyst and manager.
Escalate any missed milestone to the Regulatory Reporting Manager within 1 business day and to the Head of Compliance if the April 30 deadline is at risk.
Log the year's milestone performance for the post-cycle review.
checklist.done: milestones tracked with alerts, misses escalated within a day, and performance logged.

checklist.step: Respond to state follow-up inquiries
actions: Log every state MCAS inquiry or ratio-outlier letter in the filing tracker on receipt with the state's response deadline.
Draft responses from the pre-filed outlier explanations, with data lineage supplied by the Regulatory Reporting Manager and clearance by Regulatory Counsel where an error is conceded.
Submit within the state's deadline and file the correspondence with the filing record.
checklist.done: every state inquiry shows a logged deadline, a cleared response within it, and filed correspondence.

checklist.step: Correct and refile when errors surface
actions: On discovering a data error post-submission, quantify the impact per state and determine with the Head of Compliance which states require a corrected refiling.
Refile through the MCAS portal's resubmission route, notify affected states per their preference, and save new confirmations.
Log the correction as an exception with root cause (mapping error, extract defect, definition misread) feeding next year's procedure.
checklist.done: corrections are quantified, refiled with confirmations, and logged with root cause.

checklist.step: Analyse own ratios against the NAIC scorecard for conduct signals
actions: After the NAIC publishes the year's MCAS scorecard, compare the company's filed ratios to the industry distribution per state and line.
Feed outlier positions into the conduct-metrics monitoring (REG-054-C32) as candidate benchmarks and into procedure updates (REG-054-C30) where they signal process weakness.
Brief the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager on positions likely to attract examiner attention.
checklist.done: a scorecard comparison exists and outlier positions feed the metrics and procedure workstreams.

checklist.step: Run the post-cycle lessons review
actions: Within 60 days of the deadline, review the cycle: milestone performance, validation error patterns, inquiry themes and any refilings.
Update the MCAS Filing Procedure and the mapping document with fixes, versioned for next cycle.
Present the cycle summary to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: a post-cycle review updated the procedure and mapping with a presented summary.

checklist.step: Retain MCAS evidence
actions: File per state/line: the filed data set, submission confirmation, attestation, reconciliation and outlier explanations, labelled for 7-year retention.
Verify retrieval by state, line and data year for examiner requests.
Hold records for any state with an open market-conduct exam.
checklist.done: filing packages are labelled for 7 years and retrievable by state, line and year with exam holds applied.

testing.step: Rebuild the scope matrix independently
actions: Pull the data year's Schedule T premiums by company/state/line and the NAIC participation chart independently of the filing team.
Recompute the threshold test per cell and construct your own required-filing matrix.
Compare to the team's countersigned matrix; any cell you require that they did not is a potential missed filing and an immediate escalation.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt matrix is compared cell-by-cell with differences escalated.

testing.step: Trace every required cell to a portal confirmation
actions: For each required company/state/line cell, retrieve the MCAS portal submission confirmation with its timestamp and filing ID.
Compare each timestamp to April 30 (or the state's documented variant deadline); any later timestamp is a fail.
List cells with no confirmation as missed filings.
testing.done: every required cell shows a timely confirmation or is listed as a fail.

testing.step: Draw the data-element sample
actions: Select 5 filed state/line combinations (seeded, reproducible), covering the largest-premium state, one refiled state if any, and one life/annuity replacement-ratio state.
Within each, select 8 data elements spanning claims counts, duration buckets, lawsuits, complaints and policy counts.
Record seed, selections and dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of states and elements is drawn covering the risk-weighted combinations.

testing.step: Recompute sampled elements from source systems
actions: Re-run the element logic from the raw warehouse tables using the NAIC definitions directly — not the team's extract code — for each sampled element.
Compare recomputed values to the filed values; deviation beyond 1% is a fail, and a deviation traced to internal-vs-MCAS definition drift is a systemic finding.
Document queries and results so the recomputation is repeatable.
testing.done: every sampled element is independently recomputed with deviations classified and queries preserved.

testing.step: Verify the premium reconciliation to Schedule T
actions: Re-foot the signed reconciliation and re-tie three states' premiums to the filed Annual Statement Schedule T.
Check each >1% variance carries a documented, plausible cause.
Confirm the reconciliation was signed before submission, not assembled after.
testing.done: the reconciliation re-foots, ties to Schedule T, and pre-dates submission.

testing.step: Verify validations and outlier explanations pre-dated filing
actions: Inspect the per-state workbooks for cleared NAIC validation runs and formula-intact lineage from extract to filed value.
Check flagged ratio movements carry written business explanations dated before the submission timestamp.
Confirm the attestation record names the officer and pre-dates submission for each sampled filing.
testing.done: validations, explanations and attestations all pre-date the submission timestamps.

testing.step: Test portal access hygiene
actions: Review the MCAS portal user list against current HR records; accounts held by leavers are access exceptions.
Confirm the March 1 access-verification step was performed and logged.
Check submission confirmations were saved same-day per the procedure.
testing.done: portal users reconcile to current staff and the access-verification and same-day-save steps are evidenced.

testing.step: Review state inquiries and refilings
actions: List the year's state MCAS inquiries and verify each shows a logged deadline, a response within it, and counsel clearance where an error was conceded.
For any refiling, verify the correction was quantified, resubmitted with a new confirmation, and root-caused.
Assess whether inquiry themes were fed into the post-cycle review.
testing.done: all inquiries and refilings trace to timely, cleared, root-caused records feeding the cycle review.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception: missed cell, late submission, element deviation, definition drift, access-hygiene gap.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a date; missed filings get an immediate late-filing plan with the affected state.
Route conceded-error handling to Regulatory Counsel for the state-notification decision, documented either way.
testing.done: every exception is logged and missed filings carry an immediate state-facing plan.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds (zero missed cells, ≤1% element deviation): effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective, with the matrix trace and recomputation tables attached.
Have the Chief Audit Executive — who prepared no filing — sign the workpaper.
File it in the compliance evidence repository and report to the Head of Compliance and the conduct/risk committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and attached tables is filed and reported.

In-scope systems.value: Conduct dashboard in Power BI fed from the claims platform, policy admin, complaints case management and the contact-center platform via the enterprise data warehouse

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with metric thresholds ratified by the conduct/risk committee; re-approved at the annual metric-set review

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly cycle: data refreshed by quarter end + 10 business days, quality-checked by +15, review meeting held by +20, committee pack issued by +25 business days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Workflow reminders at each cycle milestone to the BI Developer, Data Quality Analyst and Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager; a missed milestone escalates to the Head of Compliance at +2 business days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Quarterly metric packs, threshold-breach investigations, meeting minutes and committee papers retained 6 years in the compliance evidence repository under Conduct/Metrics

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every threshold breach is logged with its investigation, root cause and remediation; missed cycle milestones and data-quality failures are logged as process exceptions

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every threshold-breach remediation and any threshold change proposed to the committee

checklist.step: Define the conduct metric set with formulas and lineage
actions: Document each metric with an exact formula: complaints per 1,000 in-force policies (by line and state), claims median/90th-percentile cycle time from report to final payment, claims denial and closed-without-payment rates, lapse rate within 24 months of issue, life/annuity replacement rate, producer terminations for cause, and complaint reopen rate.

Record the data lineage per metric: source system, warehouse table, filter logic and owner, aligning claims definitions with the MCAS definitions used in REG-054-C31 so internal and filed numbers cannot diverge silently.
Version the metric dictionary and have the Head of Compliance approve it.
checklist.done: an approved metric dictionary with formulas and lineage exists, aligned to MCAS definitions.

checklist.step: Set thresholds and benchmark sources per metric
actions: Set two limits per metric: an internal tolerance (amber) from trailing 8-quarter performance, and a regulatory benchmark (red) from external sources — NAIC MCAS scorecard averages, NAIC complaint-index conventions, and any BMA-communicated expectation.
Record the benchmark source, its publication date and refresh cadence next to each threshold.
Take the threshold set to the conduct/risk committee for ratification and minute the decision.
checklist.done: every metric carries ratified amber and red thresholds with dated, sourced benchmarks.

checklist.step: Build the data pipelines from the operational systems
actions: Build warehouse feeds from the claims platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter), policy admin, the complaints case-management queues and the contact-center platform, landing quarter-complete snapshots by quarter end + 5 business days.
Implement the metric dictionary's filter logic in versioned transformation code, not in dashboard formulas, so recomputation is possible.
Add automated reconciliation checks: complaint counts vs case-management totals, claim counts vs platform closure reports, policy counts vs in-force reports.
checklist.done: versioned pipelines land quarter-complete snapshots with automated reconciliation checks passing.

checklist.step: Build and maintain the conduct dashboard
actions: Build the Power BI conduct dashboard: per-metric trend with amber/red threshold bands, drill-down by line, state and business unit, and a benchmark-comparison page.
Drive all visuals from the warehouse metric tables — no dashboard-side recalculation of formulas.
Grant read access to the compliance, claims and distribution leadership groups via the workspace app, and version-control the dashboard definition.
checklist.done: the dashboard renders every dictionary metric with threshold bands and drill-downs, driven solely from warehouse tables.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly data refresh and quality check
actions: By quarter end + 10 business days, confirm the snapshot loaded and the automated reconciliations passed; investigate any failure with the Data Engineer before publication.
Spot-check 10 records per source (a complaint, a denied claim, a lapsed policy) from the warehouse back to the operational system screens.
By +15 business days, certify the quarter's data fit for review and log the certification in the GRC platform; late or failed certification escalates to the Head of Compliance at +2 days.
checklist.done: each quarter carries a logged data certification by +15 business days with reconciliations and spot-checks documented.

checklist.step: Hold the quarterly conduct-metrics review meeting
actions: By quarter end + 20 business days, convene the review with the Claims Director / Manager, Complaints Manager, Consumer Affairs Manager and a distribution representative.
Walk every metric against its thresholds and benchmark: confirm greens, challenge ambers, and open a formal investigation for every red.
Minute attendees, per-metric dispositions and actions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: a minuted quarterly review dispositions every metric with investigations opened for all reds.

checklist.step: Investigate every threshold breach
actions: For each red-threshold breach, open an investigation case within 5 business days of the review: drill the metric to line, state, team and time period to isolate the driver.
Pull a file sample from the affected segment (e.g. 20 denied claims, 20 complaint files) and read them against the governing procedure (REG-054-C30).
Deliver a written finding within 20 business days: driver, policyholder impact, and whether the breach signals a procedure, training, resourcing or product problem.
checklist.done: every red breach has a case opened within 5 days and a written finding within 20 business days.

checklist.step: Determine root cause and remediation for confirmed drivers
actions: For findings in claims and complaints, agree the remediation with the accountable operations owner: procedure fix, targeted retraining, staffing change or system fix, each with an owner and date.
Where policyholders were harmed, scope redress with the Claims Director / Manager and track payment through the billing platform.
Log root cause and remediation in the GRC platform against the breach record.
checklist.done: confirmed drivers carry owned remediations in the GRC record and harmed policyholders have scoped redress.

checklist.step: Escalate persistent and severe breaches
actions: Escalate any metric red for two consecutive quarters, or any breach indicating systemic unfair treatment, to the conduct/risk committee with the investigation findings.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether a persistent breach meets the material-failure test requiring BMA self-report under REG-054-C30 — record the assessment either way.
Track committee-directed actions to closure.
checklist.done: two-quarter reds reach the committee with a documented BMA self-report assessment on each.

checklist.step: Compare against external benchmarks each cycle
actions: Refresh the benchmark values when the NAIC publishes the annual MCAS scorecard and complaint-index data, recording the publication date.
Recompute the company's relative position per metric and flag movements toward the adverse tail even where internal thresholds are green.
Feed benchmark positions into the quarterly pack's comparison page.
checklist.done: benchmark values are refreshed on publication and relative positions appear in each quarterly pack.

checklist.step: Feed findings into procedures and training
actions: Route each investigation finding that implicates a written procedure to the procedure owner via the REG-054-C30 update pipeline with a due date.
Route findings implicating staff practice to the Learning & Development Specialist for targeted modules under REG-054-C29.
Verify at the next quarterly review that routed items landed — findings that vanish between cycles are the ladder's failure mode.
checklist.done: every finding routes to a procedure or training action and its landing is verified next cycle.

checklist.step: Issue the quarterly committee pack
actions: By quarter end + 25 business days, issue the conduct/risk committee pack: metric dashboard extract, threshold breaches with investigation status, benchmark positions, and remediation tracker.
Present at the committee, minute challenge and decisions, and record any threshold changes the committee ratifies.
File the pack and minutes in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: each quarter's pack is issued by +25 business days, presented, minuted and filed.

checklist.step: Run the annual metric-set review
actions: Annually, re-examine the metric set against the year's complaint themes, MCAS inquiry topics (REG-054-C31), incident learnings and any BMA or state guidance — add metrics where blind spots appeared, retire metrics no one acts on.
Re-baseline thresholds from the trailing 8 quarters and re-source benchmarks.
Take the revised set to the conduct/risk committee for ratification and re-version the metric dictionary.
checklist.done: an annually ratified, re-versioned metric dictionary reflects the year's learnings.

checklist.step: Log process exceptions on the cycle itself
actions: Log missed cycle milestones, failed data certifications and late investigations as process exceptions with root cause and owner.
Track exception trends — repeated data-quality failures mean the pipeline, not the analyst, needs fixing.
Include process-exception counts in the quarterly pack.
checklist.done: cycle failures are logged with causes and trends reported in the pack.

checklist.step: Retain metric packs and investigation evidence
actions: File each quarter's pack, minutes, breach investigations and remediation closures under Conduct/Metrics with the 6-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by quarter, metric and business unit.
Hold records tied to any open regulator engagement or redress programme.
checklist.done: packs and investigations are filed, labelled for 6 years and retrievable by quarter and metric.

testing.step: Inventory the year's cycle outputs
actions: Retrieve all four quarterly packs, review minutes, data certifications and the GRC breach records for the year.
Check each quarter met its milestone dates (+10 data, +15 certification, +20 review, +25 pack) from the logged timestamps.
Record the inventory and any missing quarter as an immediate fail.
testing.done: all four quarters' outputs are inventoried with milestone timeliness assessed.

testing.step: Reconcile pack metrics to the warehouse
actions: For one selected quarter, tie every headline metric value in the pack back to the warehouse metric tables.
Values that differ from the tables indicate manual pack edits — an integrity exception wherever found.
Verify the automated source reconciliations (complaints, claims, policy counts) passed for that quarter.
testing.done: pack values tie to warehouse tables with no unexplained manual edits and reconciliations verified.

testing.step: Draw the recomputation sample
actions: Select one quarter in depth plus 6 metrics (seeded, reproducible) spanning complaints, claims cycle time, denial rate and lapse/replacement.
Include every metric that breached red in the year.
Record seed, selections and dates.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering breached metrics and a cross-section of the dictionary is drawn.

testing.step: Recompute sampled metrics from raw operational data
actions: Recompute each sampled metric from the raw source tables using the dictionary formula directly, bypassing the production transformation code.
Compare to the published values; deviation beyond 2% is a fail, and a deviation caused by transformation code diverging from the dictionary is a systemic finding.
Verify claims-metric definitions still align with the MCAS definitions filed under REG-054-C31.
testing.done: sampled metrics recompute within tolerance with definition alignment confirmed and queries preserved.

testing.step: Verify thresholds and benchmarks were applied as ratified
actions: Compare the thresholds used in each quarterly pack to the committee-ratified set; unratified threshold changes are exceptions.
Check benchmark values cite their source and publication date, and match the NAIC's actual published scorecard figures for two spot-checked metrics.
Confirm amber/red classifications in the packs follow mechanically from the values and thresholds.
testing.done: packs used ratified thresholds, benchmarks match their sources, and classifications follow the numbers.

testing.step: Trace every red breach to an investigation
actions: For every red classification in the year, retrieve the investigation case and check it opened within 5 business days of the review and concluded within 20 business days.
Read each finding for substance: a driver identified from drill-down and file sampling, not a restatement of the metric.
Confirm remediation actions carry owners, dates and GRC records.
testing.done: every red breach traces to a timely, substantive investigation with owned remediation.

testing.step: Re-perform one breach investigation
actions: Select one concluded red-breach investigation and independently re-drill the metric and re-read a sample of the same segment's files.
Compare your driver conclusion to the recorded finding; a materially different conclusion is an exception.
Check harmed-policyholder redress from that investigation traces to actual payments in the billing platform.
testing.done: the re-performed investigation corroborates the finding (or logs the divergence) and redress traces to payments.

testing.step: Verify escalation and self-report assessments on persistent breaches
actions: Identify metrics red in two consecutive quarters and confirm each reached the conduct/risk committee with findings attached.
Retrieve the documented BMA self-report assessment for each and confirm Regulatory Counsel participated.
Verify committee-directed actions were tracked to closure.
testing.done: persistent breaches show committee escalation, a documented self-report assessment and closed actions.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception: missed milestone, manual pack edit, recomputation deviation, uninvestigated breach, missing escalation.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a date.
Flag systemic findings (transformation drift, vanishing findings) for the annual metric-set review agenda.
testing.done: every exception is logged with cause, owner and date, and systemic findings reach the annual review agenda.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the conclusion against the thresholds (four complete quarters, ≤2% recomputation deviation, all breaches investigated): effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
Have the Chief Audit Executive — who produced no pack and led no investigation — sign the workpaper.
File it in the compliance evidence repository and report to the conduct/risk committee alongside the next quarterly pack.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the conduct/risk committee.
